newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Aug gold imports tumble as demand stays weak.
newsitem.headline: Japan Aug gold imports tumble as demand stays weak.

text.p: Japan's gold imports tumbled in August from year-earlier levels because weak demand from both the investment sector and the jewellery industry showed no sign of recovering, traders said on Monday.

In addition to fragile demand, a lack of inflationary concerns in the United States, perceptions that there was little chance of dollar-based gold prices rising, and higher yen-based gold retail prices encouraged those with gold holdings to sell in order to take profits, they said.
"Constant profit-taking selling by private investors who bought gold at much lower retail prices also depressed gold demand," an official at a bullion house said.
The official said profit-taking has overwhelmed buying in the physical gold market in recent months.
Japan's gold imports in August totalled 9.53 tonnes, down 54.1 percent from a year earlier, Finance Ministry data released on Monday showed.
Imports in the first eight months of 1996 totalled 105.08 tonnes against 199.47 tonnes in the same period last year.
One trader said gold imports in calendar 1996 could fall 50 percent from 262.30 tonnes in 1995 if the situation continues.
